A Note on Additive Complements

Fang-Yu Ma

Abstract: Two infinite sequnences AA and BB of non-negative integers are called additive complements, if their sum contains all sufficiently large integers. Let A⁡(x)A(x) and B⁡(x)B(x) be the counting functions of AA and BB. In this paper, we extend the results of Liu and Fang in 2016 and obtain some results on additive complements. For example, we prove that there exsit additive complements AA and BB such that lim supx→+∞A⁡(x)​B​(x)x=2\displaystyle\limsup_{x\rightarrow+\infty}\dfrac{A(x)B(x)}{x}=2 and A⁡(x)​B​(x)−x=1A(x)B(x)-x=1 for infinitely positive integers xx.

1 Introdution

Two infinite sequnences AA and BB of non-negative integers are called additive complements, if their sum A+B={a+b:a∈A,b∈B}A+B=\{a+b:a\in A,b\in B\} contains all sufficiently large integers. Let A⁡(x)A(x) and B⁡(x)B(x) be the counting functions of AA and BB, namely

A⁡(x)=∑a∈Aa≤x1andB⁡(x)=∑b∈Bb≤x1.A(x)=\displaystyle\sum_{a\in A\atop a\leq x}1\quad\text{and}\quad B(x)=\displaystyle\sum_{b\in B\atop b\leq x}1.

In 1964, Danzer [1] conjectured that for additive complements AA and BB, if

lim supx→+∞A⁡(x)​B​(x)x≤1,\displaystyle\limsup_{x\rightarrow+\infty}\dfrac{A(x)B(x)}{x}\leq 1,

then

A⁡(x)​B​(x)−x→+∞asx→+∞.A(x)B(x)-x\rightarrow+\infty\quad\text{as}\quad x\rightarrow+\infty.

In 1994, Sa´\acute{a}rko¨\ddot{o}zy and Szemere´\acute{e}di [2] proved the conjecture. Fang and Chen [3, 4] proved the following result: for additive complements AA and BB, if

lim supx→+∞A⁡(x)​B​(x)x>2orlim supx→+∞A⁡(x)​B​(x)x<3−3,\displaystyle\limsup_{x\rightarrow+\infty}\dfrac{A(x)B(x)}{x}>2\quad\text{or}\quad\displaystyle\limsup_{x\rightarrow+\infty}\dfrac{A(x)B(x)}{x}<3-\sqrt{3},
††footnotetext: 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification: Primary 11B13, 11B34.  Keywords. Additive complements, Counting functions, Upper limit.

then

A⁡(x)​B​(x)−x→+∞asx→+∞.A(x)B(x)-x\rightarrow+\infty\quad\text{as}\quad x\rightarrow+\infty.

On the other hand, Chen and Fang [5] proved the following result.

Theorem A. For any integer aa with a≥2a\geq 2, there exist additive complements AA and BB such that

lim supx→+∞A⁡(x)​B​(x)x=2​a+2a+2\displaystyle\limsup_{x\rightarrow+\infty}\dfrac{A(x)B(x)}{x}=\frac{2a+2}{a+2}

and A⁡(x)​B​(x)−x=1A(x)B(x)-x=1 for infinitely positive integers xx.

In 2016, Liu and Fang [6] extended the above result and proved the following result.

Theorem B. For any integer a,ba,b with 2≤a≤b2\leq a\leq b, there exist additive complements AA and BB such that

lim supx→+∞A⁡(x)​B​(x)x=2a−1a​b−1+1\displaystyle\limsup_{x\rightarrow+\infty}\dfrac{A(x)B(x)}{x}=\frac{2}{\frac{a-1}{ab-1}+1}

and A⁡(x)​B​(x)−x=1A(x)B(x)-x=1 for infinitely positive integers xx.

In this paper, we extend Theorem B and prove the following results.

   Theorem 1.1.

There exist additive complements AA and BB such that

lim supx→+∞A⁡(x)​B​(x)x=2\displaystyle\limsup_{x\rightarrow+\infty}\dfrac{A(x)B(x)}{x}=2

and A⁡(x)​B​(x)−x=1A(x)B(x)-x=1 for infinitely positive integers xx.

   Theorem 1.2.

There exist additive complements AA and BB such that

lim supx→+∞A⁡(x)​B​(x)x∈(169,2)\ℚ\displaystyle\limsup_{x\rightarrow+\infty}\dfrac{A(x)B(x)}{x}\in(\frac{16}{9},2)\backslash\mathbb{Q}

and A⁡(x)​B​(x)−x=1A(x)B(x)-x=1 for infinitely positive integers xx.

Let

ℒ=\displaystyle\mathcal{L}= {lim supx→+∞A⁡(x)​B​(x)x:A,Bare additive complements,A(x)B(x)−x=1for infinitelyx},\displaystyle\left\{\displaystyle\limsup_{x\rightarrow+\infty}\dfrac{A(x)B(x)}{x}:A,B\ \text{are additive complements,}\ A(x)B(x)-x=1\ \text{for infinitely}\ x\right\},

and ℒ′\mathcal{L}^{{}^{\prime}} be the derivative of ℒ\mathcal{L}, that is, the set of all the clusterpoints of ℒ\mathcal{L}. By Theorem A and Theorem B, we have 2∈ℒ′.2\in\mathcal{L}^{{}^{\prime}}.

   Theorem 1.3.

For any integer a,ba,b with b>a≥2b>a\geq 2 and b≥a+2b\geq a+2, we have 21+ab⁡(a+1)∈ℒ′.\dfrac{2}{1+\frac{a}{b(a+1)}}\in\mathcal{L}^{{}^{\prime}}.

   Lemma 3.1.

Next we prove the uniqueness. Assume that m=∑j=0nεjaj=∑i=0kεi′ai,εn≠0,εk′≠0m=\displaystyle\sum_{j=0}^{n}\varepsilon_{j}a_{j}=\displaystyle\sum_{i=0}^{k}\varepsilon_{i}^{{}^{\prime}}a_{i},\varepsilon_{n}\neq 0,\varepsilon_{k}^{{}^{\prime}}\neq 0. Proof of Lemma 2.12.1  For any positive integer xx, if x∉A∪Bx\notin A\cup B, then
